issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is inconsistent between the problem statement (instructions and UML) and the solution implementation. The problem statement instructs students to follow the UML order when implementing the constructor (problem_statement.md lines 16-21). The UML in the problem statement lists attributes in this order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors (problem_statement.md lines 63-68). The solution implements the constructor as: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13), placing lectureName first and swapping the positions of numberOfLecturers and numberOfGuestStudents relative to the UML. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct constructor signature and can cause automated tests that verify parameter order to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent between the UML/problem statement and the implementation. Two options: (A) Change the solution constructor signature to match the UML order, e.g. public Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors) and adjust the assignments inside the constructor and any tests accordingly; or (B) If the solution's parameter order (String lectureName first) is intentional, update the problem statement and the UML to list the parameters in that same order and update any tests/instructions that assert a specific order. Also ensure the template (if it provides a constructor) matches the chosen order.
